items.title: Oil tops $100 a barrel, Houthi attack in Red Sea marks new escalation
items.content: US strikes on Iran ongoing after Tehran attacked ships in Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices surged above $100/barrel. Houthi attacks in Red Sea mark new escalation in the conflict.

items.title: Iran Digs In After Latest Trump Threat on Civilian Targets
items.content: Iran IRGC said one of three oil tankers trying to pass through mined route south of Strait of Hormuz caught fire after explosion. Other two tankers turned back. Strait remains effectively blocked.

items.title: Despite June MoU to reopen Strait of Hormuz, Iran continues to assert hegemonic control
items.content: The June 2026 memorandum of understanding aimed to reopen the Strait and end the Iran war, but Iran persists in asserting control and attempting to collect fees on ships passing through.

items.title: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
items.content: Disruptions to shipping through Strait of Hormuz and heightened geopolitical risk in the Gulf are impacting global markets including oil prices, shipping costs, and real estate markets.

items.title: Stock market July 24: S&P 500 flat, Nasdaq drops as oil surge weighs on tech
items.content: S&P 500 closed at 7,411.98 (+0.05%). Dow gained 235.60 points (+0.46%) to 51,947.25. Nasdaq dropped 0.64% to 24,975.82. NDX RSI at 41 (bearish), SOX RSI at 47. Margin debt remains elevated.

items.title: Stocks Stabilize Early as Oil Prices Retreat
items.content: US markets attempting to stabilize but NDX RSI at 41 and SOX RSI at 47 signal bearish headwinds. Margin debt remains elevated, adding to pressure if markets continue sagging.

items.title: HSI Jumps 1.28% to 25,210.81 on Tech and Travel Strength
items.content: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index climbed 1.28% to close at 25,210.81 on July 23, driven by gains in technology shares and encouraging corporate news from the travel sector.

items.title: HSI Jumps Over 2% as State Buying Lifts Hong Kong Stocks
items.content: HSI rose 2.36% to 25,143, reclaiming 25,000 level and 50-day MA. Rally followed ~¥60 billion in purchases by Chinese state-backed investment platforms.

items.title: US June CPI expected to ease to 3.5% from 4.2%, first slowdown in 5 months
items.content: US annual inflation rate expected to ease to 3.5% in June 2026 from 4.2% in May, first slowdown in five months. Monthly CPI forecast to edge down 0.1%, first decline since May 2020.

items.title: Bank of America CEO warns inflation will back Fed into a corner
items.content: BofA CEO Brian Moynihan warns inflation remains sticky. Fed projects 2026 headline PCE of 3.6% and core PCE of 3.3% (median). Fed held rates at 3.50%-3.75% for 4th straight meeting.

items.title: China's largest memory chipmaker CXMT stokes fears of cash drain ahead of IPO
items.content: CXMT's blockbuster stock market debut could pull cash from China's equities market. Chip sector facing overvaluation concerns despite Beijing's support.

items.title: China equities extend rebound, led by AI and semiconductor shares
items.content: Chinese stocks rose, led by AI and semiconductor shares, as investor sentiment remained upbeat following gains marking the sharpest rally in three months.

items.title: Earnings this week: Alphabet, Tesla, Intel headline Q2 results
items.content: Week of July 20-24 saw wave of Q2 earnings from Alphabet, Tesla, and Intel. Next week (July 27-31): Microsoft and Apple earnings are the key events.

items.title: Earnings Calendar July 27-31: Microsoft, Apple, Meta in focus
items.content: Next week's earnings include Microsoft (AI business robustness vs capex concerns), Apple (solid 2026 run, briefly surpassed Nvidia as biggest stock), and other mega-cap tech.

items.title: Weekly commentary: Middle East escalation - markets less reactive but fewer buffers
items.content: BlackRock notes markets have reacted less sharply to latest Middle East escalation, yet the global economy has fewer buffers against a prolonged energy shock than in prior cycles.
